title: What Happens When You CRACK Your Knuckles? 💥
description:
You lock your fingers, push... and CRACK. No bones were harmed.

Each knuckle is a joint sealed in a bag of slippery fluid, and that fluid has gas dissolved in it, a bit like a sealed can of soda. Pull the joint apart and the pressure inside drops, so the gas suddenly comes out as a bubble. In 2015, scientists filmed a finger being pulled inside an MRI scanner: the bubble appeared at the very moment of the crack. (Whether the noise is the bubble forming or the bubble partly collapsing is still argued.) Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

Will it give you arthritis? Dr. Donald Unger cracked the knuckles of his left hand, and never his right, at least twice a day for 50 years: no arthritis in either hand, and an Ig Nobel Prize in 2009. Bigger studies have found no link with arthritis either. Bonus: a knuckle can't crack again for about 20 minutes, while the gas dissolves back.
